mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 1.2 million units.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% MoM signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO drops > 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 1 quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 1 quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tight labor market with potential inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3% and UNRATE < 4%.
